name: 麺屋武蔵 神山
address_ja: 〒101-0047 東京都千代田区内神田3-8-7 グラン・フォークス神田ビル 1F
cuisine: The Kanda branch of the Menya Musashi group — a double soup of chicken-and-pork stock married to katsuobushi and niboshi, poured over thick noodles and topped with the house 蒲焼きチャーシュー: pork belly steamed for hours to render the fat, marinated in tare, then finished under a salamander so it crisps like grilled eel. Ramen and tsukemen (plain, rich, spicy), roughly ¥1,000–¥1,900.
neighborhood: Uchi-Kanda 3-chōme — 2 min from Kanda station's west exit (JR Chūō / Yamanote / Keihin-Tōhoku), 4 min from Kanda on the Tokyo Metro Ginza line (exit 1), 6 min from Shin-Nihombashi on the Sōbu line
gf_detail: Not workable for coeliac. Wheat noodles are the dish; the group's own page for Kanzan describes a shōyu-based double soup and a chāshū marinated in tare (wheat soy sauce) before grilling. No gluten-free claim, no rice-noodle option and no allergen chart anywhere on menya634.co.jp.
vegan_detail: Animal from the ground up — the soup is chicken carcass and pork bone plus bonito flake and niboshi, and every bowl on the Kanzan board is built on it. There is no vegetable soup and no vegan topping set.

roles: 麺屋武蔵グループ (Menya Musashi Co., Ltd.) — group branch; individual branch chef not named publicly
chef_bio.origin: Nishi-Shinjuku — the group's 総本店 opened there in 1996
chef_bio.background: Kanzan is one of fourteen Tokyo shops in the Menya Musashi group, which opened its first store in Nishi-Shinjuku in 1996 and is routinely filed in Japanese ramen writing among the 「96年組」, the 1996 cohort credited with turning ramen from a counter trade into a service business. The group's own vision page makes that the whole argument: before 1996, it says, the ramen shop was 「主」 — the master cooked, and if the bowl was good then a dirty room and brusque service were considered beside the point; Musashi's founding idea was 「食べる喜びのあるラーメン屋を作りたい」, a shop where the pleasure is the whole visit rather than only the soup. Every branch carries its own name and its own bowl instead of a chain recipe — 二天 in Ikebukuro fries pork and chicken tempura into it, 虎洞 in Kichijōji makes a chāshū sausage, 武骨 in Okachimachi runs white/black/red tonkotsu — and Kanzan, opened in Kanda in 2009, is the one that does the kabayaki chāshū. The group also runs shops in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Singapore, China, Ukraine, Los Angeles, Indonesia and Seattle. No individual chef is named for the Kanda branch on the company site.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「革新にして上質」 and 「お客様に喜んでいただく」 — innovation and quality judged by the customer's whole experience rather than the bowl alone. The company writes that a recipe is only a score, and that the cooking depends on who plays it.
chef_bio.specialty: 蒲焼きチャーシュー — pork belly long-steamed to drop the fat, tare-marinated, then crisped under a salamander in the manner of grilled eel, over the 二刀流 double soup (animal stock plus katsuobushi and niboshi).

anecdotes.text: Menya Musashi's own vision page claims the shop as a turning point in ramen history: 「今でも日本のラーメンの歴史を、大きく変えたエポックメーカーの“96年組”と言われております」.
Tabelog reviewers warn that the map pin is a block off — 「食べログの地図だと、路地一本ズレていて」 — so navigate by the street address (内神田3-8-7) rather than by the pin.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: menya634.co.jp's Kanda store page gives the address 東京都千代田区内神田3-8-7 グラン・フォークス神田ビル, the 2009 opening, weekday 11:00–22:30 / weekend 11:00–22:00 hours, no closing day, and the kabayaki-chāshū description. Tabelog 13061115 confirms the same address and phone (03-3256-3634), 17 counter seats, all non-smoking, a ¥1,000–¥1,999 band, and 1,046 ratings at 3.42. Gnavi 41fd91bd0000 independently lists 〒101-0047 内神田3-8-7 and 神田駅西口 徒歩1分. The GSI address-search API geocodes 内神田3-8-7 to 139.76973, 35.691032 — within ~20 m of the Tabelog coordinates used here.

gf_cross_contamination.text: A 17-seat wheat-noodle counter. Noodles are boiled in a shared pot and the whole menu is ramen or tsukemen; there is nothing wheat-free on it and no allergen handling is published.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Shōyu tare and a tare-marinated chāshū. Ordinary wheat soy sauce must be assumed — no tamari is named anywhere on the group's site.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Chicken-and-pork stock combined with katsuobushi and niboshi is the base of every bowl.

positives.text: The group's service-first founding philosophy means staff are unusually attentive by ramen-counter standards, so a question asked at the ticket machine will at least be heard out — but nothing published suggests they can answer it with a wheat-free bowl.

cultural_comfort.note: Ticket-machine ordering, counter only, 17 seats, a queue at lunch. Menya Musashi is one of the most foreigner-familiar ramen groups in Tokyo — the corporate site runs in five languages and there are branches in Seattle and Los Angeles — so pointing at a button works fine. It is two minutes from Kanda's west exit, but Tabelog's pin sits one alley off; walk to 内神田3-8-7. Solo diners are the norm.

enrich_note: Confirmed. The light record's name 「麺屋武蔵 神山」 is exactly right; Kanzan is the group's Kanda branch. Verified against the group's own store page, Tabelog 13061115 and Gnavi 41fd91bd0000, all giving 千代田区内神田3-8-7. The approximate pin (35.6918, 139.771) was ~150 m northeast of the real shop; coordinates replaced with Tabelog's shop coordinates, which the GSI address geocoder corroborates to within ~20 m.

name: 味噌ラーメン＆つけ麺 麺処 神田
address_ja: 〒101-0047 東京都千代田区内神田3-20-6 Kanda ex 1F
cuisine: A 12-seat miso counter one minute from Kanda's north exit: thick, high-viscosity miso soup with a hard salt edge, mid-thick noodles and a stack of very thick chāshū — free extra vegetables, extra garlic and a small rice come with the ticket. Bowls run roughly ¥900–¥1,250 (味卵味噌チャーシュー麺 ¥1,250).
neighborhood: Uchi-Kanda 3-chōme — 1 min from JR Kanda station's north exit (Yamanote / Chūō / Keihin-Tōhoku)
gf_detail: Not workable. Miso ramen is the entire menu — wheat noodles in a shared pot, and miso tare that in a shop of this style is normally cut with soy sauce; nothing gluten-free is claimed and no allergen sheet exists. Assume wheat in the noodles, the tare and the chāshū marinade.
vegan_detail: Pork-forward by design: the selling point is a stack of thick pork chāshū on a pork-and-miso soup, with a marinated egg on the flagship bowl. No vegetable broth, no vegan option.

chef_bio.background: A newcomer rather than an institution — the shop opened in 2023 on the Kanda side street behind the north exit and was written up that September by the ramen site Ramental as 「神田の新店」. It is a plain, cheap, high-volume miso counter of twelve seats, all non-smoking, ticket machine at the door, open from eleven in the morning to midnight seven days a week, which in an office district like Kanda means it catches the late shift as much as the lunch rush. Reviewers describe the bowl as deliberately unsubtle: thick, viscous, salt-forward miso, mid-thick noodles with enough backbone to survive it, and a visually startling pile of thick-cut chāshū, with free 野菜・ニンニク増量 and a small rice thrown in — the 'obviously filling' school of ramen rather than the refined one. No owner is named on any listing and the shop keeps no website; ordering, menu and communication all run through the ticket machine and a delivery page.
chef_bio.specialty: 味卵味噌チャーシュー麺 (¥1,250) — miso ramen with a marinated egg and a stack of thick-cut chāshū, with free vegetable and garlic increase.

anecdotes.text: A 2026 Tabelog reviewer notes the ticket machine prints 「味卵」 while the single-item menu says 「味玉」 — a small inconsistency regulars find funny — and that staff ask at hand-over whether you want the vegetables and garlic doubled.
The shop was covered as a Kanda new opening by ramental.net in September 2023.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13288962 gives 千代田区内神田3-20-6 Kanda ex 1F, tel 03-6690-8551, 12 counter seats, all non-smoking, a ~￥999-and-under price band, 11:00–24:00 every day with 1/1 and 1/2 closed, JR神田駅北口 徒歩1分, and 276 ratings at 3.52. Ramendb (s/152540) and Ramental list the same shop as 「麺処 神田」; Uber Eats and Retty list it under the fuller signboard name 「味噌ラーメン＆つけ麺 麺処 神田」, which is what the light record was echoing. GSI geocodes 内神田3-20-6 to 139.771133, 35.69289 — ~25 m from the Tabelog coordinates.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Twelve seats, one noodle pot, a menu that is wheat noodles and nothing else. No allergen information published anywhere.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Miso tare in this style of shop is normally cut with soy sauce, and the chāshū is tare-braised. Wheat must be assumed; no tamari is claimed.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Pork stock, pork chāshū and marinated egg are the point of the bowl.

cultural_comfort.note: Ticket machine, twelve counter stools, no English signage reported and no website. One question does get asked out loud at hand-over — whether you want the free vegetable and garlic increase — so a nod covers it. The compensation is the hours: open until midnight seven days a week, and a Tabelog reviewer found it half-empty at 22:10 on a weekday, which makes it one of the easier late meals near Kanda station.

enrich_note: Confirmed. The light record's 「味噌ラーメン つけ麺 麺処 神田」 is the shop's full signboard name, which Uber Eats and Retty render as 「味噌ラーメン＆つけ麺 麺処 神田」 and which Tabelog and Ramendb shorten to 「麺処 神田」 — same business, 内神田3-20-6, opened 2023. name: 鮮魚らーめん 五ノ神水産
address_ja: 〒101-0046 東京都千代田区神田多町2-9-6 田中ビル別館 1F
cuisine: 「魚を飲んでみませんか？」 — a fish-obsessed ramen bar whose signature soup, 銀だら搾り, is made from roasted silver cod and water and nothing else: ¥1,000 for the ramen, ¥1,300 for the crab-pressed tsukemen, ¥1,000 for the lobster-tomato tsukemen, ¥900 for shrimp abura-soba, with egg and extra-meat tiers on top.
neighborhood: Kanda Tachō 2-chōme — 4 min from Awajichō (Tokyo Metro Marunouchi line) and Ogawamachi (Toei Shinjuku line), 6 min from JR Kanda's north exit
gf_detail: Not workable, despite an unusually clean base. The 銀だら搾り broth genuinely is roasted silver cod and water — but the noodles are wheat, made by the group's own 五ノ神製麺所, and neither the tare nor the tsukemen dipping liquor is published as wheat-free. There is no gluten-free claim and no allergen sheet on gonokamiseisakusho.com.
vegan_detail: The entire concept is fish. Silver cod, crab, lobster and shrimp are the four soups; chāshū and marinated egg are the standard toppings. There is nothing plant-based on the board.

roles: 株式会社五ノ神製作所 (Gonokami Seisakusho Co., Ltd.) — group-operated; branch chef not named publicly
chef_bio.origin: Shinjuku — the group's first shop, つけ麺 五ノ神製作所, is in Shinjuku Sanchōme
chef_bio.background: Gonokami Suisan is the fish arm of the Gonokami Seisakusho group, whose Shinjuku original built its name on a lobster-and-tomato tsukemen and which now runs its own noodle factory, 五ノ神製麺所, and a shop in Taiwan. The Kanda branch states its concept in four words on its own page — 「魚を飲んでみませんか？」, would you like to drink a fish — and follows it literally: the house soup, 銀だら搾り, is roasted silver cod and water, with no stock animal behind it. That produces a bowl reviewers describe as aggressively, almost confrontationally fishy; Ramen Walker filed its television segment under 「やり過ぎ“たら”美味かった」, roughly 'they overdid the cod and it was delicious'. The rest of the board rotates other shellfish through the same idea — a crab-pressed tsukemen, the group's lobster-tomato tsukemen, a shrimp-oil abura-soba, and limited runs like a gindara 'junk' bowl with baked cheese rice. Fifteen seats, counter-led, a Tabelog score of 3.71 across 1,517 ratings. No individual chef is named; the company publishes a monthly all-store operating calendar instead, which is the honest signal that the hours move.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「魚を飲んでみませんか？」 — a soup that is the fish itself rather than a fish note laid over an animal base.
chef_bio.specialty: らーめん銀だら搾り ¥1,000 (roasted silver cod and water); つけ麺蟹搾り ¥1,300; オマール海老トマトつけ麺 ¥1,000; 海老油そば ¥900.

anecdotes.text: A Tabelog reviewer went for the crab-pressed tsukemen, saw the 「鮮魚ラーメン」 sign and admits to thinking 「鮮魚…ラーメン？ｗ」 before reading the shop's 'drink a fish' concept line.
Ramen Walker covered the shop on television as 「やり過ぎ“たら”美味かった衝撃の新感覚麺」.
The parent company posts a fresh 「全店舗営業予定」 calendar at the end of every month — the closing days genuinely move, and the shop's X account is the stated place to check.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: gonokamiseisakusho.com/kanda.html carries the concept line 「魚を飲んでみませんか？」, the 銀だら搾り description (roasted silver cod and water only) and the full priced menu quoted above. Tabelog 13163444 gives 千代田区神田多町2-9-6 田中ビル別館1F, tel 03-6206-8814, 15 seats (11 counter plus two 2-tops), all non-smoking, Wednesday and Sunday closed with 不定休, and the Awajichō/Ogawamachi 4-min access. Gnavi er7dvbtp0000 lists it independently at 淡路町駅 徒歩2分. GSI geocodes 神田多町2-9-6 to 139.768631, 35.693966 — ~20 m from the Tabelog coordinates.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Wheat noodles from the group's own 五ノ神製麺所, boiled in a shared pot; the whole menu is noodles. No wheat-free preparation is offered or claimed.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: No tamari is named. The tare and the tsukemen dipping liquor should be assumed to contain wheat soy sauce even though the base soup itself is only cod and water.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Silver cod, crab, lobster and shrimp are the four soups; there is no plant-based bowl and no vegan topping.

positives.text: Unusually transparent about the base: the shop states plainly that 銀だら搾り is roasted silver cod and water, which is more than most ramen counters will tell you about what is in the pot.

cultural_comfort.note: Fifteen seats, counter-led, and a menu the shop itself prints with English glosses (Ramen silver cod squeezing, Tsukemen crab squeezed) — awkward English, but enough to order by. The real friction is the hours: Wednesday and Sunday off plus genuine 不定休, so check the company's monthly calendar or the shop's X account before travelling. Come at lunch or right at 17:00; the mid-afternoon gap is real.

enrich_note: Confirmed. Light record read 「五ノ神水産」; the shop's own page and signboard read 「鮮魚らーめん 五ノ神水産」, the same business with its full prefix restored — not a garbling. Verified on the operator's own site (gonokamiseisakusho.com/kanda.html), Tabelog 13163444 and Gnavi er7dvbtp0000, all at 千代田区神田多町2-9-6. The light record filed it under 神田; it is in fact nearer Awajichō/Ogawamachi. Approximate pin was ~200 m east; coordinates replaced with the shop's, corroborated to ~20 m by the GSI geocoder.

name: ギャラリー珈琲店 古瀬戸
address_ja: 〒101-0051 東京都千代田区神田神保町1-7 ＮＳＥビル 1F
cuisine: A 1988 Jimbōchō kissaten that doubles as a rental gallery — red walls, blue ceiling, a four-year mural finished in 1992, charcoal-roasted single-origin coffee from Hagihara Coffee in Kobe (straight coffee about ¥700), three curries, sandwiches, and the house cheese-custard choux cream; chiffon cake ¥650 with ¥100 off as a set. Cash only.
neighborhood: Kanda-Jimbōchō 1-chōme, on the book-shop street — 1 min from Jimbōchō station (Toei Mita / Toei Shinjuku / Tokyo Metro Hanzōmon lines, exit A5)
gf_detail: Coffee is safe; nothing on the food side is. The kitchen's three signatures are Japanese-style curry (roux-thickened with wheat flour in this genre — no flour-free version is claimed), sandwiches on bread, and wheat-flour bakery — chiffon cake and choux pastry. No gluten-free claim, no allergen sheet, and no separate preparation is described anywhere on the shop's own site, on Tabelog or in the Santatsu feature. Come for the coffee and the room, eat elsewhere.
vegan_detail: Black coffee and tea only. The curries include a beef curry; the cakes and choux are built on egg, butter and cheese custard; the sandwiches are dairy-and-egg territory. No plant milk is advertised and no vegan item appears on any published menu. A vegan can sit here happily with a straight coffee — that is the whole of it.

chef_bio.chef_name: 加藤 (Katō) — owner; 桜井美智子 (Michiko Sakurai), shop manager
chef_bio.origin: Jimbōchō, Chiyoda-ku — the sister shop 古瀬戸珈琲店 opened nearby in 1980
chef_bio.background: Koseto opened in 1988 as the gallery-bearing sister of 古瀬戸珈琲店, which the same owner had started in 1980 a few streets away in the same Jimbōchō book district. The owner, Katō, built it on a single idea — 「アートを日常に」, art in ordinary life — and then commissioned the room to prove it. The exterior mural was painted by Ōe Akiyo while she was still a student at Tokyo University of the Arts and an acquaintance of the owner; the interior wall was painted by 鬼頭まあこ (Maako Kido) over four years and finished in 1992, with her piece 「浮かぶ桃」 partly repainted around 2011. The red walls are not decoration but working gallery surface: the shop rents them out by section, with a semi-private area given over to exhibitions full-time, and photographers and painters have shown there for decades. Regulars point out that red walls are unusual in galleries but standard in museums, which is why the work hangs well. The coffee is charcoal-roasted beans from Hagihara Coffee in Kobe, poured as house blends and as straights — the mochas get singled out for depth. Manager Sakurai Michiko runs the floor and describes the customers, with the mildness of someone who has watched a book district's readers for years, as 「素敵な方々」. Seventy seats, all non-smoking, open every day, cash only, no Wi-Fi — a deliberate refusal of the laptop café.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「アートを日常に」 — art brought into the everyday, so that a cup of coffee is taken inside a working gallery rather than beside a poster.
chef_bio.specialty: Charcoal-roasted Hagihara straight coffee (~¥700); cheese-custard choux cream; chiffon cake ¥650; three curries.

anecdotes.text: The interior mural took the painter Maako Kido four years and was completed in 1992; her 「浮かぶ桃」 was partly repainted around 2011.
The exterior wall was painted by Ōe Akiyo, then a student at Tokyo University of the Arts and a friend of the owner.
The red walls are rented out to exhibitors by section — regulars note that red is rare in galleries but standard in museums, and that pictures hang unusually well on them.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: The shop's own site (gallerykoseto.shopinfo.jp) gives the address 東京都千代田区神田神保町1-7, phone 03-3294-7941, 10:00–20:00 年中無休, cash only, no Wi-Fi, fully non-smoking, and describes the room as 「アートに包まれた空間です」 with the Kido murals and a rotating hang. Tabelog 13011635 confirms the same address in the ＮＳＥビル 1F, 70 seats, a 1988 opening, a ~￥999 price band, 神保町駅 徒歩1分, and 412 ratings at 3.57 — but lists Thursday as 10:00–18:00 against the site's flat 10:00–20:00, hence hours_status 'irregular'. Santatsu (san-tatsu.jp/articles/381815) carries the 1980/1988 sister-shop history, the owner Katō, the manager Sakurai Michiko, both muralists, the Hagihara Coffee sourcing and the gallery-rental model. GSI geocodes 神田神保町1-7 to 139.759201, 35.695789 — ~20 m from the Tabelog coordinates.

gf_cross_contamination.text: A kissaten kitchen turning out curry, sandwiches, chiffon cake and choux pastry — wheat flour is in continuous use in a small space, and no wheat-free handling is described.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Not a soy-sauce kitchen, but Japanese-style curry roux is itself wheat-flour-based; that, not shōyu, is the gluten route here.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Beef curry on the menu; the pastry is cheese custard, egg and butter. No plant milk is advertised.

positives.text: Straight charcoal-roasted coffee, poured black, is a genuinely safe order for both diets — and the room is the reason to come.

cultural_comfort.note: A walk-in kissaten one minute from Jimbōchō station, seventy seats, open every day from ten to eight, entirely non-smoking. Bring cash — no cards — and do not expect Wi-Fi; this is a room for reading, which suits the book district it sits in. Ordering is straightforward pointing, and lingering over one coffee is the accepted behaviour rather than a transgression. Combine it with the second-hand bookshops on Yasukuni-dōri.

enrich_note: Confirmed. The light record's name 「ギャラリー珈琲店 古瀬戸」 is exact and matches Tabelog 13011635 and the shop's own site. Note there are two related shops in Jimbōchō under the Koseto name — this one (ギャラリー珈琲店 古瀬戸, 神田神保町1-7, opened 1988) and its 1980 elder sibling 古瀬戸珈琲店 (Tabelog 13006272); Gnavi lists both. Coordinates moved from the neighbourhood centroid to the shop's own, corroborated to ~20 m by the GSI geocoder for 神田神保町1-7. GF downgraded from the light record's 'ask' to 'no': every food item published is wheat-based.

name: こってりらーめん なりたけ TOKYO 錦糸町店
cuisine: The Tokyo flagship of a Chiba 背脂チャッチャ house: simmered pork back-fat shaken through a flat strainer over the bowl (the chatcha sound is where the style's name comes from), on a heavy shōyu or miso soup with firm, wavy medium-thick house noodles. 醤油らーめん ¥1,000, 味噌らーめん ¥1,050, 特製みそつけめん ¥1,100; back-fat volume is set to taste, gyōza ¥400, weekday lunch set ¥250. Open until three in the morning.
neighborhood: Kinshi 3-chōme — 3 min from JR Kinshichō station's north exit (Sōbu line) and from Kinshichō on the Tokyo Metro Hanzōmon line
hours_raw: 月・火・木・金・土・日 11:00～翌3:00　水曜定休
gf_detail: Not workable. The noodles are wheat and made in the company's own factory in Inage; the company's own menu page describes the tsukemen dough as one where 「噛みしめれば小麦の香りが広がる」 — the wheat is the selling point. Both soups are shōyu- or miso-tare based with pork back fat; no gluten-free claim, no allergen chart on naritake.co.jp.
vegan_detail: Pork back fat is the entire concept, over a pork-and-chicken soup, with chāshū and marinated egg as toppings and gyōza on the side. There is no vegetable option; even the fish-dashi bowl (a Chiba-branch exclusive, not served here) is built on a pork/chicken/niboshi triple stock.

roles: founder of 有限会社なりたけ
chef_bio.origin: Funabashi, Chiba — the company office is still at 前原西 in Funabashi
chef_bio.background: Naritake was founded on 1 March 1996 by a man named Narita, who trained at 'Ramen Benkei' before opening his own shop; the name is simply his surname. Twenty-nine years on, 有限会社なりたけ is a seventy-person company running five directly-operated shops — Tsudanuma, Motoyawata, Makuhari and a Fukuoka branch in Nishijin, plus this one, the Tokyo flagship, opened in Kinshichō in 2009 and the only Tokyo address the company lists. The house style is 背脂チャッチャ: pork back fat, simmered and then shaken vigorously through a flat strainer held over the bowl, so it falls in a snow of emulsified fat — the chatcha is the noise the strainer makes, and it is what the style is named after. The noodles are wavy medium-thick and made daily at the company's own factory in Inage, developed specifically to carry that much fat without collapsing. Ordering is by fat level; the shop is orange-signed, counter-only, and open from eleven in the morning until three the following morning, which is what makes it a Kinshichō institution rather than merely a good bowl — it is the last hot thing available on that side of the river. The brand has since opened in Paris.
chef_bio.philosophy: Unapologetic 背脂こってり: rich by intention, with the fat level handed to the customer as a dial rather than hidden.
chef_bio.specialty: 醤油らーめん ¥1,000 — the shop's most-ordered bowl, a clean-edged shōyu soup carrying the back-fat richness; 味噌らーめん ¥1,050; 特製みそつけめん ¥1,100, three misos and more than ten ingredients and spices blended into a pork-bone dipping sauce.

anecdotes.text: The founder trained at 'Ramen Benkei' before opening the first Naritake in 1996; the shop carries his own surname.
Kinshichō was the brand's first Tokyo shop, opening in 2009, and remains the only Tokyo address on the company's store list.
The company's own menu page notes that 背脂 can be dialled to taste on the standard bowl, and left out entirely on the miso tsukemen — 「背脂無しも選べます」.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: naritake.co.jp/company gives 有限会社なりたけ, founded 平成8年3月1日 (1 March 1996), office at 千葉県船橋市前原西2-34-9-102, 70 staff, five directly-run shops, and lists 錦糸町店 at 東京都墨田区錦糸3-3-2 — the sole Tokyo location. naritake.co.jp/menu carries current prices (醤油 ¥1,000, 味噌 ¥1,050, 特製みそつけめん ¥1,100, ぎょうざ ¥400, ランチセット ¥250 to 15:00 weekdays) and the in-house noodle description. Tabelog 13116484 lists 「なりたけ TOKYO 錦糸町店」 at the same address, tel 03-5637-7456, counter-only seating, 11:00–翌3:00 with Wednesday closed, 錦糸町駅北口 徒歩3分, and 1,286 ratings at 3.59. Santatsu (san-tatsu.jp/articles/218403) supplies the 2009 Tokyo-flagship opening, the founder's Benkei training, the Inage noodle factory and the chatcha etymology. GSI geocodes 錦糸3-3-2 to 139.813507, 35.698071 — within ~5 m of the Tabelog coordinates.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Wheat noodles from the company's own Inage factory, boiled in a shared pot; gyōza wrappers in the same kitchen. Nothing wheat-free is offered.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Both flagship soups are shōyu- or miso-tare based and the miso tsukemen sauce blends three misos with ten-plus ingredients. No tamari is named; assume wheat throughout.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Pork back fat is shaken over every standard bowl and the stock is pork and chicken. Chāshū, marinated egg and gyōza are the toppings and sides.

positives.text: One genuinely useful control for a sensitive stomach, though not for gluten: the back-fat quantity is adjustable to taste, and the miso tsukemen can be ordered 背脂無し.

cultural_comfort.note: Counter-only, orange sign, no English menu published. The one thing you will be asked is how much 背脂 you want — 「普通」 for normal, 「少なめ」 for less — and getting that question right is most of the transaction. Open to 3am six days a week (closed Wednesdays), three minutes from Kinshichō's north exit, so it is the reliable late meal in a district where most kitchens shut at eleven. Expect a queue at peak lunch and after midnight on weekends.

enrich_note: Confirmed. Light record read 「なりたけ TOKYO 錦糸町店」, which is exactly how Tabelog 13116484 names it; the company's own store list calls the same shop simply 錦糸町店 and the brand signboard is 「こってりらーめん なりたけ」, so the name has been given here in full. Verified on naritake.co.jp (company page listing 東京都墨田区錦糸3-3-2 as the only Tokyo shop), on Tabelog and in a Santatsu feature. Approximate pin was ~150 m off; coordinates replaced with the Tabelog shop coordinates, which the GSI geocoder for 錦糸3-3-2 matches to ~5 m.

name: タイ国料理レストラン タイランド
cuisine: Kinshichō's veteran Thai house, open since August 1986 and run as the direct restaurant arm of a Thai-food import trader — vegetables, fish and seasonings flown and shipped in from Thailand, with a Thai kitchen and Thai floor staff. Green curry, tom yum goong, som tam thai with the heat set to order, Thai suki; Thai-style ramen ¥850, som tam ¥1,100, yam nua ¥1,350, steamed sea bass with lemon ¥2,350. Budget around ¥2,000–¥3,000 at dinner.
neighborhood: Kinshi 3-chōme, on the Kinshi Park side — 3 min from Kinshichō on the Tokyo Metro Hanzōmon line (exit 4), 5 min from JR Kinshichō's north exit, 1 min from the Kinshi-kōen-mae bus stop
gf_detail: Genuinely worth asking, but nothing is claimed. Thai cooking gives you a real starting hand — som tam, yam nua, tom yum goong and the curries are rice-and-fish-sauce dishes rather than wheat ones, and the restaurant imports its own seasonings from Thailand rather than substituting Japanese ones, which lowers the odds of wheat shōyu creeping in. Against that: soy sauce, oyster sauce and seasoning sauce are standard in a Thai kitchen and most Thai brands contain wheat; the menu carries a Thai-style ramen and fried items; and no allergen information is published on Tabelog, Hot Pepper or Gnavi. The owner's stated habit of explaining dishes to customers who do not know Thai food is the opening — ask which dishes use シーユー/オイスターソース before ordering.
vegan_detail: Fish sauce (ナンプラー) and dried shrimp are the backbone of Thai seasoning and are almost certainly in the som tam and the curry pastes; the green curry will normally carry chicken and fish sauce. There is no published vegetarian or vegan section. A Thai kitchen with Thai staff can usually build a vegetable dish to order — 「ジェー」 (jay) is the word — but this shop makes no such claim, so treat it as a conversation, not an option.

roles: operated as the direct restaurant arm of a Thai food import trading company
chef_bio.origin: Shizuoka Prefecture (b. 12 June 1969); the restaurant has been in Kinshi 3-chōme since 1986
chef_bio.background: Thailand opened in August 1986, which makes it older than the 'Little Thailand' reputation Kinshichō later acquired — by the time Japanese media started writing about the Thai bars and grocers clustered around the station, this restaurant had already been feeding the neighbourhood for two decades. It is not an independent's kitchen but the直営 restaurant of a Thai-food import trading company, and Suzuki is candid that this is the point: the vegetables, the fish and the seasonings come in by air and sea from Thailand, the kitchen and the floor are staffed by Thai cooks and servers, and what lands on the table is meant to be what would land on a table in Bangkok rather than a Japanese reading of it. Suzuki, from Shizuoka and born in 1969, describes his own job as translation more than cooking — 「タイ料理を分かっていない方が多いので、丁寧に説明するようにしている」 — talking customers through unfamiliar dishes so they can find a way into them, and setting the chilli on the som tam to whatever the diner can actually take. His personal motto, given to a Sumida ward profile, is a single word: 「バランス」. Fifty to sixty seats over a wide, unhurried room that takes groups; in a 2012 interview the shop's small boast was that it stocked large bottles of Singha shipped straight from Thailand when almost nowhere in Tokyo did.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「バランス」 — and authenticity as a supply chain rather than a slogan: import the ingredients, hire the cooks, then explain the food to whoever walks in.
chef_bio.specialty: Green curry and tom yum goong (the two perennials), som tam thai with adjustable heat, Thai suki, steamed sea bass with lemon ¥2,350, yam nua ¥1,350.

anecdotes.text: Suzuki on the operation: 「タイ食材の商社の直営で、厨房もサービスもタイ人スタッフ」 — the restaurant is run by the importer, with a Thai kitchen and Thai floor staff.
In a 2012 ward interview the shop's distinguishing detail was large bottles of Singha imported direct from Thailand — a rarity in Tokyo at the time.
AERA's 【昭和な名店】 feature files it as the Kinshichō place to eat Thai street food that Japanese diners have not met.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13002968 gives 東京都墨田区錦糸3-12-10, tel 03-3626-3885, an August 1986 opening, 50 seats, a ¥2,000–¥2,999 band, Monday closed, and 560 ratings at 3.49, with the Hanzōmon-line exit-4 3-min / JR north-exit 5-min / Kinshi-kōen-mae bus 1-min access. Hot Pepper strJ000128909 lists the same address with 60 seats and a later 23:00 close, which is why hours are marked irregular. Gnavi 4ybzmu7k0000 files it as 「レストランタイランド」 at 錦糸町駅4番口 徒歩3分. The Sumida ward business profile (sumida-jikan.com) names the proprietor 鈴木庸一, born 12 June 1969 in Shizuoka, and carries the import-trading-company background, the Thai staffing, the signature dishes and the 「バランス」 motto. GSI geocodes 錦糸3-12-10 to 139.814178, 35.699108 — within ~10 m of the Tabelog coordinates.

gf_cross_contamination.text: A 50–60 seat general Thai kitchen with a noodle dish and fried items on the menu; no separate wheat-free preparation is claimed and no allergen sheet is published.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Thai seasoning sauces — light soy (สีอิ๊ว), oyster sauce, seasoning sauce — normally contain wheat, and this kitchen imports Thai brands rather than substituting Japanese ones, so the question is which dishes use them, not whether the shop stocks them. Nothing is published either way.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Fish sauce and dried shrimp are standard in som tam and in curry pastes; the green curry is normally chicken. No vegetarian or vegan menu section exists.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The proprietor's own stated practice is to explain dishes carefully to customers unfamiliar with Thai food, and som tam heat is adjusted on request — evidence that a dietary conversation will be entertained, though not that it will be guaranteed.

positives.text: Rice-based cuisine with an imported Thai larder and a Thai kitchen brigade: the raw odds of an accidental wheat dish are lower here than at a Japanese-style izakaya, and there are naturally wheat-free candidates on the board (som tam, yam nua, tom yum goong).

cultural_comfort.note: A forty-year-old neighbourhood restaurant rather than a scene — fifty-odd seats, wide tables, groups welcome, lunch service from 11:30 and a break in the afternoon on weekdays but straight through at weekends. Thai floor staff and an owner whose declared habit is explaining the food make this an unusually good room in which to ask a question in imperfect Japanese or English. Closed Mondays. It sits on the Kinshi Park side of the station, in the same few blocks as Kinshichō's Thai grocers and bars.

enrich_note: Confirmed, and not a generic phrase despite appearances. 「タイランド」 is the actual registered shop name — Tabelog 13002968 files it under exactly that single word — while Gnavi lists the same business as 「レストランタイランド」 and the Sumida ward profile as 「タイ国料理レストラン『タイランド』」; the full form is used here. Same address, phone and 1986 opening across all three. Approximate pin was ~250 m away; coordinates replaced with the shop's, corroborated to ~10 m by the GSI geocoder for 錦糸3-12-10. GF and vegan both left at 'ask' as the light record had them — the cuisine is promising, the shop publishes nothing, and the owner is on record as willing to talk diners through the menu.

name: CLANN BY THE RIVER
address_ja: 〒135-0024 東京都江東区清澄1-1-7 LYURO 東京清澄 by THE SHARE HOTELS 2F
cuisine: A waterfront all-day restaurant on the second floor of the LYURO hostel, with a wood terrace straight onto the Sumida — soup-led breakfast from 7am (clam chowder or a seasonal vegan soup, both ¥1,650 as a set), Texas pulled-pork and fried-horse-mackerel burgers at lunch (¥1,400–¥1,500), craft beer and natural wine from Fujimaru's Kiyosumi winery in the evening. Bread from Chigaya in Kuramae, coffee from Leaves Coffee Roasters. Cashless only; dogs welcome on the terrace.
neighborhood: Kiyosumi 1-chōme on the Sumida riverbank — 10 min from Kiyosumi-shirakawa (Toei Ōedo / Tokyo Metro Hanzōmon lines, exit A3), 10 min from Suitengūmae (Hanzōmon line, exit 4)
gf_detail: One genuinely labelled gluten-free item and a wheat-heavy kitchen around it. The published menu lists a 「VEGAN / GLUTEN FREE COOKIE」 (¥450) among the sweets — from the vegan brand GUGGA, which supplies CLANN's baked goods and its soups — and the rest of the board is waffles, Chigaya bread, burger buns, tortilla chips, fried chicken, fish nuggets and French fries out of a shared fryer. That is a claim scoped to a bought-in product while wheat is worked continuously on the premises, so it does not lift the shop above 'ask'. No allergen sheet is published and no wheat-free preparation is described. The seasonal vegan soup set comes with 「RICE or BREAD」 — take the rice and ask what is in the soup.
vegan_detail: Real, published, and not an afterthought. The shop's own concept page states it offers a soup breakfast that 「ベジタリアンの方も“Choice”できる」, and the morning menu carries a 「SEASONAL VEGAN SOUP SET」 (¥1,650) built as vegan soup + salad + rice or bread + soy-milk yoghurt + drink. The soups are produced for CLANN by GUGGA, a vegan sweets and recipe brand, and GUGGA's baked goods are sold on site — including a vegan soft cookie and a vegan/gluten-free cookie at ¥450. Beyond breakfast, the plant-based picks are tortilla chips with salsa and guacamole (¥880), house pickles (¥600), carrot and purple-cabbage rapée (¥500) and mixed nuts (¥550), and the entire wine list is natural wine. What is not established: whether the soup stock, the salad dressing and the bread are free of dairy and egg on any given day — ask, since the soup is seasonal and the menu PDF dates from December 2022.

roles: restaurant attached to LYURO 東京清澄 by THE SHARE HOTELS; head chef not named publicly
chef_bio.origin: Kiyosumi, Kōtō-ku — on the Sumida at the old Kiyosu bridge side
chef_bio.background: The restaurant opened on 14 April 2017 as PITMANS, a smokehouse-and-craft-beer room on the second floor of LYURO, the riverside hostel THE SHARE HOTELS converted from an office building on the Sumida. On 1 December 2022 it was renamed CLANN BY THE RIVER — clann being the Irish word the operators gloss as 「家族、血筋、血縁、仲間、愛する人」, chosen for a place they wanted loved across generations. The pulled pork and the smoker survived the rebrand; what was added was a local supply chain declared on the front page as 「LOCAL FIRST」. The bread is from Chigaya in Kuramae, the coffee beans from Leaves Coffee Roasters in the same district, the wine from Fujimaru's winery which is itself in Kiyosumi-shirakawa — and every wine on the list is natural. The soups, both the Kiyosumi clam chowder and the seasonal vegan one, are produced by GUGGA, a vegan brand better known for its cookies, which also develops plant-based recipes for other companies. The room's real asset is the wood terrace over the river, which is public space the restaurant does not control — you take a seat first and order at the till afterwards — and which is one of the few dog-friendly waterfronts in central Tokyo, with water and treats kept behind the bar. It took a Gault & Millau 2020 POP-category award. Payment is cashless, full stop: cards, IC, QR, no yen notes. No chef is named on the site; the identity is built on the suppliers instead.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「LOCAL FIRST」 — 「ローカルに愛されてこそ、グローバルに愛される」, plus fair trade and 'brewery to table'; Kuramae bread, Kuramae coffee, Kiyosumi wine, and soups designed by a vegan brand.
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal vegan soup set (¥1,650, breakfast) and Kiyosumi clam chowder; Texas pulled-pork burger ¥1,500; fried-horse-mackerel fish burger ¥1,500; waffle fried chicken ¥1,400; GUGGA vegan and vegan/gluten-free cookies ¥450.

anecdotes.text: The rename was explained in the hotel's own notice: 「『CLANN』には、「家族、血筋、血縁、仲間、愛する人」などの意味があります」 — a place meant to be loved across generations. PITMANS became CLANN on 1 December 2022.
The terrace is public land: 「テラスは公共の場となっております。CLANNではお座席、場所の管理を行っておりません」 — secure your own seat before you order, or they cannot serve you.
All three signature suppliers are neighbours — Chigaya bread and Leaves Coffee from Kuramae, and Fujimaru, whose winery is in Kiyosumi-shirakawa itself.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: clannbytheriver.jp (which pitmans.jp now 301-redirects to) gives the address 〒135-0024 東京都江東区清澄1丁目1-7 LYURO 東京清澄 by THE SHARE HOTELS 2F, tel 050-3188-8919, hours 7:00–22:00 (L.O. 21:00), the 10-minute walks from Suitengūmae exit 4 and Kiyosumi-shirakawa exit A3, the cashless-only policy, the LOCAL FIRST / FAIRTRADE / BREWERY TO TABLE concept, the Chigaya, Leaves Coffee and Fujimaru sourcing, the dog-friendly terrace, the Gault & Millau 2020 POP award, and the statement that the soup breakfast is one 「ベジタリアンの方も“Choice”できる」. The linked menu PDF (clann_menu20221201.pdf) carries the full priced board in Japanese and English, including the SEASONAL VEGAN SOUP SET and the VEGAN / GLUTEN FREE COOKIE. Tabelog 13207479 confirms the address, the 14 April 2017 opening, 50 seats, tel 03-5875-8953, a ¥3,000–¥3,999 band and 866 ratings at 3.49. THE SHARE HOTELS' own news post dates the PITMANS→CLANN rename to 1 December 2022. GSI geocodes 清澄1-1-7 to 139.792007, 35.681087 — within ~10 m of the Tabelog coordinates.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Waffles, Chigaya bread, burger buns and a fryer running fried chicken, fish nuggets and chips. Shared equipment throughout; no allergen sheet and no wheat-free preparation is described.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Not a shōyu kitchen in the main — the food is American/European-leaning — but the gapao rice at lunch is a Thai dish that normally uses soy and oyster sauce, and nothing is published about which sauces are used.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The kitchen also handles pulled pork, fried chicken, clam chowder and fish. The vegan items are cooked in the same room, and the menu does not state whether the seasonal vegan soup shares equipment.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Ordering is by QR code from your seat indoors, or at the till on the terrace — which makes a spoken dietary question slightly harder than usual. Ask at the register before you scan.

positives.text: Items are labelled in English and Japanese on the published menu, and VEGAN and GLUTEN FREE appear as explicit product labels rather than as inference — rare in a Tokyo all-day restaurant.
A dedicated seasonal vegan soup set with soy-milk yoghurt at breakfast, designed by a vegan brand, plus an all-natural wine list.

cultural_comfort.note: About as low-friction as central Tokyo gets: bilingual printed menu, QR-code ordering from the table indoors, English on the board, and an all-day 7:00–22:00 service so there is no closed window to plan around. Two things to know before you go — it is cashless (cards, Suica/PASUMO, QR; no cash at all), and the river terrace is public space you must claim yourself before ordering at the till. Dogs are welcome on the terrace but not inside. It is a genuine ten-minute walk from either station, along the water.

enrich_note: Confirmed. Light record's 「CLANN BY THE RIVER」 is exact; Gnavi still carries the 旧PITMANS tag, and the shop's old domain pitmans.jp 301-redirects to clannbytheriver.jp. Verified on the restaurant's own site and menu PDF, on Tabelog 13207479 and in THE SHARE HOTELS' rename announcement. Approximate pin was ~700 m northeast; coordinates replaced with the shop's, corroborated to ~10 m by the GSI geocoder for 清澄1-1-7. Vegan raised from the light record's 'ask' to 'options' on the strength of a published seasonal vegan soup set and GUGGA-supplied vegan baked goods; GF left at 'ask' — the one gluten-free item is a bought-in cookie in a kitchen that fries and bakes wheat all day. Caveat for the merge: the only menu the shop publishes is dated 1 December 2022, so prices and the seasonal soup should be treated as indicative.

name: カラシビ味噌らー麺 鬼金棒 神田本店
address_ja: 〒101-0044 東京都千代田区鍛冶町2-10-9
cuisine: The original 15-seat counter of Tokyo's kara-shibi house: a miso built on Shinshū miso from casks nearly a century old, blended with cheese, peanut paste, nam pla and spices, laid over a ten-hour pork-and-chicken stock doubled with fish, then wok-fired to order — with 「カラ」 (chilli) and 「シビ」 (Wakayama budō-sanshō and Sichuan huājiāo oil) each dialled from none to 増し, or 鬼増し for ¥200 more. カラシビ味噌らー麺 ¥1,080; つけ麺 ¥1,130 (Kanda only); 特製 ¥1,830.
neighborhood: Kajichō 2-chōme — 2 min from Kanda station on the Tokyo Metro Ginza line, 3 min from JR Kanda's east or north exit, 4 min from Iwamotochō (Toei Shinjuku line)
gf_detail: Ruled out by the shop's own allergen chart, which is the good news here — Kikanbo publishes a per-item 特定原材料 analysis (revised 8 April 2026) and every らー麺 and every つけ麺 on it is marked 小麦. Below the table it states plainly that the same production line handles wheat among other allergens and that 「調理には同じ調理器具を使用しますので、調理の過程でアレルギー物質が微量に混入する可能性が稀にあります」. The noodles are a custom three-gauge wheat blend and the miso itself is a soy-and-wheat-fermented base. There is no wheat-free bowl and the shop does not pretend otherwise.
vegan_detail: No — and specifically no even for the vegetables. The house miso blend itself contains cheese and ナンプラー (fish sauce), the double soup is pork bone, chicken carcass and fish, and the chāshū is star-anise kakuni. The unmarked toppings on the allergen chart (もやし, パクチー, ヤングコーン, ねぎ, のり, 卓上スパイス) are plant items, but they are only ever served into that soup.

chef_bio.chef_name: 三浦正和 (Masakazu Miura) — 代表取締役
roles: representative director, 株式会社鬼金棒
chef_bio.origin: Kanda Kajichō, Chiyoda-ku — the first shop, and still the head office
chef_bio.background: Kikanbo opened its first kara-shibi miso shop in Kanda in September 2009: nine tsubo of floor, nine counter seats, and a proposition — ramen you experience through all five senses, built on chilli heat (カラ) and sanshō numbing (シビ) — that the Japanese ramen trade had not seen packaged that way before. A limited-run tsukemen in November 2010 drew a response far beyond what the shop expected and became a second Kanda storefront in its own right. 株式会社鬼金棒 was incorporated in October 2011 under 三浦正和; a second Tokyo shop followed in Ikebukuro in July 2014, and in March 2015 the brand went abroad, opening two Taipei shops on the same day. It now runs in Taiwan, Hong Kong, Melbourne and Singapore, and next door at 鍛冶町2-10-10 keeps 鬼金棒Lab, an experimental storefront for new bowls. The cooking is more elaborate than the counter suggests: the miso is a base of Shinshū miso from wooden casks used for close to a hundred years — the shop credits the 樽ぐぜ, the flavour the cask itself has taken on — layered with selected cheeses, peanut paste, fish sauce and spices and kneaded in stages; the shibi oil is Wakayama budō-sanshō and Sichuan huājiāo drawn slowly at low temperature; the noodles are three separate gauges cut on custom blades and blended in one bowl; and the miso, aromatics and chilli are stir-fried over high heat in a wok for each individual order. The star-anise braised chāshū is described in the shop's own copy as a 「甘いオアシス」 in the middle of the heat. The Kanda flagship closed for nine days in September 2025 for a refit and reopened.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「一日一変化」 — a change a day; ramen as a five-senses experience, with the customer setting the heat and the numbing rather than the kitchen.
chef_bio.specialty: カラシビ味噌らー麺 ¥1,080, with カラ and シビ each selectable 抜き／少なめ／普通／増し and 鬼増し at +¥200; カラシビ味噌つけ麺 ¥1,130, sold only at the Kanda flagship; 特製 ¥1,830; 肉々 ¥2,320.

anecdotes.text: The first shop was nine tsubo with nine counter seats, and the company's own history says the concept 「業界に大きなインパクトを与えた」 — it hit the trade hard.
The tsukemen exists because a limited-time run in November 2010 drew a response 「予想を遥かに上回る」 and had to be given its own shop.
The miso base comes from Shinshū casks used for nearly a century, and the shop credits the wood itself — 「木樽の“樽ぐぜ”に育まれた」 — before listing the cheese, peanut paste and nam pla layered into it.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kikanbo.co.jp's company page gives 株式会社鬼金棒, incorporated October 2011, capital ¥10m, 30 staff (November 2025), representative director 三浦正和, and a dated history: first Kanda shop September 2009, Kanda tsukemen shop November 2010, Ikebukuro July 2014, Taipei March 2015. Its shop page lists 神田本店 at 東京都千代田区鍛冶町2-10-9, tel 03-6206-0239, 11:00–21:30 Mon–Sat and holidays, 11:00–16:00 Sunday — with 鬼金棒Lab and the head office next door at 2-10-10. The menu page carries current prices and the miso, noodle, spice and double-soup descriptions. The linked allergen PDF (制作日 2026年4月8日) marks 小麦 on every noodle item and states the shared-line and shared-equipment caveats. Tabelog 13097205 confirms the address, phone, 15 counter seats, a 17 September 2009 opening, 無休, and 2,788 ratings at 3.72. Gnavi 1kby0v7t0000 lists it independently at 神田駅3番口 徒歩2分. GSI geocodes 鍛冶町2-10-9 to 139.772461, 35.69368 — within ~5 m of the Tabelog coordinates.

gf_cross_contamination.text: The shop's own allergen sheet marks 小麦 on every ramen and tsukemen item and warns that the same line produces wheat-containing products and that the same cooking equipment is used, so trace transfer is possible.
Noodles are a custom three-gauge wheat blend — the whole texture concept depends on them.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The base is a miso blend (soy and wheat fermented) further layered with fish sauce and spices; no tamari or wheat-free seasoning is claimed anywhere.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The miso blend itself contains cheese and nam pla; the double soup is pork bone, chicken and fish; the chāshū is braised pork. Nothing served is free of animal products.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The chart is a theoretical ingredient analysis and the shop says so: 「詳細に原材料調査を行った理論上のもので、お客様のアレルギー症状が発症しないことを保証するものではありません」. Honest, and correctly framed — but it is not a guarantee.

positives.text: A per-item allergen table across 29 declarable ingredients, dated and revised (8 April 2026), published free as a PDF from the menu page — better disclosure than most Tokyo restaurants of any size offer, and it makes the 'no' verdict here evidence-based rather than assumed.
Both the chilli and the sanshō can be ordered 抜き (none), which matters for anyone who cannot take the spice even though it does nothing for gluten.

cultural_comfort.note: Fifteen counter seats, ticket-first, and a queue most of the day — Kikanbo is one of Kanda's best-known bowls and the flagship is small. The one exchange you must handle is the heat: カラ and シビ are each set 抜き／少なめ／普通／増し, and 「普通」 is already assertive by non-Japanese standards; 鬼増し is a challenge, not a default. The company runs an English page and shops in Melbourne and Singapore, so foreign customers are routine. Open seven days, but Sunday closes at 16:00. 鬼金棒Lab, the experimental sibling, is literally next door at 2-10-10 if the queue is impossible.

chef_bio.chef_name: さいとう (Saitō) — the shop carries the proprietor's surname; no fuller name is published
chef_bio.origin: Kanda Toyamachō, Chiyoda-ku; the cooking is Hakata-style
chef_bio.background: Tempura Saitō opened on 21 January 2016 in a small building off the east side of Kanda station, and it argues its case in one sentence on its own front page: have you never eaten tempura at home or in a restaurant and found it soggy and disappointing? The fix, it says, is not exotic — thin house batter, good oil, and above all the refusal to do what other shops do, which is fry everything and then bring the whole plate. 「他店のように、すべてが揚がってからご提供することは、ありません」. Each piece comes as it leaves the oil. That is a Hakata habit rather than an Edo-mae one, and so is the rest of the operation: the lunch teishoku with bottomless rice, miso soup, shiokara and pickles, which is exactly how the Fukuoka tempura counters run, and a Hakata mizutaki on the dinner menu beside the tempura courses. Twenty seats — twelve at the counter and two four-tops — with all courses including all-you-can-drink and the whole room bookable for twenty seated or twenty-five standing, which is what it mostly does with its evenings in an office district. Lunch is cash only and takes no reservations. Nobody's cooking biography is published; the shop's identity is the frying method and the Hakata format.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「薄い衣で 揚げたてで 美味しい天ぷらを」 — thin batter, fried to order, served one piece at a time rather than as a finished tray.
chef_bio.specialty: さいとうオールスター定食 ¥1,600 (whole prawn, squid, pork fillet, chicken breast and thigh, two seasonal vegetables); さいとう定食 ¥1,200; とり天定食 ¥1,250 — Hakata's chicken tempura; 博多名物水炊き on the dinner courses.

anecdotes.text: The shop's own directions are the most useful thing on its site: out of Kanda's east exit, cross at the lights, take the lane between the soba shop Kameya and the Nanboya buy-back store, straight on, then left at the corner where the izakaya Kokoro stands — and it is in front of you.
Lunch teishoku come with free refills of rice, miso soup, shiokara and pickles — 「食べ放題」, spelled out on the shop's own front page.
Every dinner course includes all-you-can-drink, and the 20-seat room takes private bookings up to 20 seated or 25 standing.

name: 神田 うな正
address_ja: 〒101-0047 東京都千代田区内神田3-11-1 三惠ビル 1F
cuisine: A 1983 Kanda eel house one minute from the station's west exit, doing Kantō-style unagi properly — split down the back, white-grilled, steamed, then grilled again — with a house tare kept deliberately light on sugar so the fish tastes of itself. うな丼 ¥1,100, うな重 ¥1,500–¥3,400, and the shop's own invention うな丼ダブル ¥2,000, two layers of eel with rice between them. Bentō from ¥1,100 to take away; free soup with a lunchtime bentō and free large rice for students.
neighborhood: Uchi-Kanda 3-chōme, on the Kanda-nishiguchi shōtengai — 1 min from JR Kanda's west exit (Yamanote / Chūō), 3 min from Kanda on the Tokyo Metro Ginza line (exit 1)
gf_detail: Worth one specific question. Kabayaki tare is soy sauce, mirin and sugar — wheat, and it is brushed on every donburi and jūbako in the house; the shop's own copy calls it 甘さ控えめの自家製ダレ but says nothing about the soy sauce in it, and no tamari is claimed. What raises this above a flat 'no' is that 白焼 (shirayaki — eel grilled plain, taken with wasabi and salt) and 素焼 are both on the à-la-carte list, so an unglazed eel genuinely exists here. The caveats are real: the same grill carries tare-basted eel all day, the 肝吸い soup and the pickles are of unstated seasoning, and nothing is published about allergens. Ask for 白焼き and ask what goes with it.
vegan_detail: A single-ingredient eel restaurant. The à-la-carte list is liver, liver skewers, rib, fin rolls, u-maki (egg roll with eel) and uzaku (eel with cucumber in vinegar); the only plant items on it, shishitō and shiitake, are grilled alongside eel. There is nothing to eat here as a vegan.

roles: 亭主 (owner-chef) — butchers the eel himself; name not published
chef_bio.origin: Uchi-Kanda 3-chōme, on the Kanda west-exit shopping street since 1983
chef_bio.background: Una-shō has been on the Kanda west-exit shōtengai since 1983, and the thing it wants you to know is what happens at three in the morning. Its own site describes the hour: the street that is busy with people all day has gone quiet, the domestic eel that came up from Shizuoka that same day is waiting, and the proprietor butchers it himself. From there the cooking is the orthodox Kantō sequence — 背開き, split along the back rather than the belly; a first white grilling; steaming, which is what makes Tokyo eel soft where Kansai eel is crisp; and then a second grilling with the tare. The house tare is made in the shop and kept 甘さ控えめ, low on sugar, on the argument that the point is the eel's own flavour rather than the glaze. Prices are the other half of the reputation: an unagi-don at ¥1,100 in central Tokyo is startling in an era when a proper Edo-mae eel lunch runs to five figures, and the shop's signature 「うな丼ダブル」 at ¥2,000 — rice, eel, more rice, more eel, stacked in two layers — is the sort of thing that gets it filmed by YouTubers rather than reviewed by critics. Thirty seats over two floors: ten at the counter downstairs, a twenty-seat tatami koagari up. It runs as 有限会社うな正, takes bulk bentō and party bookings with two days' notice, gives a free clear soup to anyone buying a bentō before two o'clock, and gives students a free large rice on production of a student card. It closes when the eel runs out.
chef_bio.philosophy: Kantō method done straight — back-split, white-grilled, steamed, re-grilled — with a low-sugar house tare so the eel, not the glaze, is what you taste; and priced for a Kanda office worker rather than for an occasion.
chef_bio.specialty: うな丼ダブル ¥2,000 — two layers of eel with rice between them; うな丼 ¥1,100; うな重 梅/竹/松/特上 ¥1,500/¥2,300/¥2,800/¥3,400; うなぎのお茶漬け ¥1,500; 白焼・素焼 on the à-la-carte board.

anecdotes.text: The shop's own account of its day: 「AM3:00。人通りで賑わう神田西口商店街は鳴りを潜め、その日に静岡から直送された国産うなぎを亭主自ら捌きます」.
Buy a bentō before 14:00 and the clear soup is free; show a student card and the large rice is free too.
The kitchen closes when the eel is gone — 「鰻が売切れ次第閉店」 — so the evening service is not guaranteed.

cultural_comfort.note: A no-frills old shop on a shopping street, one minute from Kanda's west exit, with a Japanese-only site and no English menu published. It is very easy at lunch — walk in, order うな丼 or うな重, eat at the counter — and the queue moves. Two practical points: the eel sells out and the shop shuts when it does, so a late-evening visit is a gamble; and Sunday and public holidays are closed, with Saturday lunch only. If you want the shirayaki, ask early in the service. Bulk bentō and party bookings need two days' notice by phone in Japanese.

address_ja: 〒101-0028 東京都千代田区神田花岡町1-19
cuisine: A Tabelog Ramen Hyakumeiten shop in the arches right outside Akihabara's central gate — a clear animal-and-niboshi shōyu finished with a late niboshi infusion, four kinds of chāshū (two shoulder cuts, belly, chicken thigh), ginger-scented wontons, kujō negi and menma; a tsukemen the shop pushes just as hard, and a shirunashi tantanmen. Around ¥1,100–¥1,500 a bowl. A hidden button on the ticket machine swaps in hand-kneaded 手揉み麺.

chef_bio.chef_name: 本田裕樹 (Yūki Honda) — founder; left the company on 1 April 2026
roles: founder and 店主 of 麺処 ほん田 (2008–2026)
representative of the operating company until April 2026
chef_bio.origin: Higashi-Jūjō, Kita-ku — where the first shop opened on 15 February 2008
chef_bio.background: Yūki Honda opened Mendokoro Honda in Higashi-Jūjō on 15 February 2008, aged twenty-one. He had drifted into ramen rather than chosen it — as a high-school student he took a job at 牛久大勝軒 partly because the dress code was lax — but he spent three years there under Kōji Tashiro, alongside Osamu Tomita of Chūka Soba Tomita, then two years adrift in Tokyo and one more training inside Tashiro's group before opening his own place. What he put out at twenty-one was, for 2008, startling: a 香味鶏だし that carried enormous umami in a clear soup, and low-temperature rare chāshū, neither of which was standard then. Twelve years and a permanent hour-long queue later, JR approached him about the arches beside Akihabara station; he took it in April 2020 for three reasons he stated plainly — the wait was unfair to customers, he wanted premises with no landlord-imposed restrictions, and he wanted a kitchen big enough to make his own noodles. He also closed the book on the old recipes: 「東十条の味は完結」, a full menu redesign, in-house noodles, and a base price raised to ¥1,100. The Akihabara shop entered Tabelog's Ramen Hyakumeiten and sits at 3.83 across 3,667 ratings. In February 2026 the business began its nineteenth year — and on 1 April 2026 the shop's official X account announced that Honda was leaving the company 「新しい挑戦と今後の展開を見据えて」. A regular who happened to eat there on 31 March records that it was Honda's last day at the stove and that he had deliberately not announced it in advance. The shop continues under its staff; when this record was written the Akihabara flagship was trading normally. Do not expect to find Honda behind the counter.
chef_bio.philosophy: Clarity with weight — a soup that reads clean but carries depth, rebuilt from scratch rather than carried over when the shop moved. Honda's stated reason for moving was to stop making customers queue an hour and to control his own kitchen.
chef_bio.specialty: 醤油 — four chāshū (two shoulder-roast cuts, belly and chicken thigh) with menma and kujō negi, finished with a late niboshi infusion; the ginger-heavy wontons; the tsukemen; 汁なし担々麺; and a 手揉み麺 (hand-kneaded noodle) swap available from a ticket-machine button most first-timers miss.

anecdotes.text: Honda took his first ramen job at 牛久大勝軒 as a high-schooler largely because the shop was relaxed about appearance, and ended up training three years under Kōji Tashiro alongside Osamu Tomita of Tomita.

JR approached him about the Akihabara arches; he moved in April 2020 to end the hour-long queues, escape landlord restrictions and get a kitchen large enough to make his own noodles — and declared the Higashi-Jūjō flavours finished.
A regular who ate there on 31 March 2026 discovered it was Honda's final service; the shop's X account announced his departure the next morning, and he had chosen not to say so beforehand.

The ticket machine hides a 手揉み麺 changeover button — reviewers report finding it only after seeing hand-kneaded noodles in other people's photographs. Buy the ticket before you join the queue; people who queue first get sent back.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13246285 gives 千代田区神田花岡町1-19, tel 070-7793-3979, an opening date of 15 April 2020 with the note 「2008年2月15日、東十条で創業」, 18 seats (4 counter, two 4-tops, three 2-tops), a ¥1,000–¥1,999 band, 11:30–15:00 and 18:00–21:00 with Wednesday closed, 秋葉原駅中央改札口より徒歩0分, and 3,667 ratings at 3.83 with Ramen Hyakumeiten status. Ramen Walker's interview (article/4010215) carries Honda's age, the 2008 founding at twenty-one, the 牛久大勝軒 apprenticeship under 田代浩二 alongside 富田治, the reasons for the April 2020 move, the in-house noodle production and the ¥1,100 base price. The shop's official X account (@T_N_W2020HONDA) announced on 1 April 2026 that 代表の本田が会社を離れる; a same-week eyewitness account by the Tabelog reviewer Dales Mivis dates his last service to 31 March 2026 and quotes the current 醤油 at ¥1,200. 千代田区観光協会 also lists the shop. gf_cross_contamination.text: Noodles are made in-house on the premises, so wheat flour is handled daily in the same kitchen that plates every bowl; wontons add wheat wrappers. No allergen information is published.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The flagship bowl is a shōyu. No tamari is named anywhere; assume ordinary wheat soy sauce in the kaeshi and in the chāshū braise.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Animal stock with niboshi, four chāshū, wontons, marinated egg and back fat on the hand-kneaded version.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Ordering is entirely by ticket machine before you join the queue, and the shop is at capacity most of its service — there is very little opportunity for a dietary conversation.

cultural_comfort.note: One of the easiest Hyakumeiten shops to reach and one of the harder ones to get into. It is under the arches directly outside Akihabara's central gate — first-timers walk past it; the queue is the landmark. Buy your ticket from the machine BEFORE joining the line, or you will be sent back to do it; seating is provided for roughly fifteen of the waiting. Expect twenty-plus people at peak, moving in about twenty minutes. Eighteen seats, mostly tables rather than counter, which is unusual and makes it workable for two. Closed Wednesdays, and there is a three-hour afternoon break. Note that founder Yūki Honda left in April 2026; the bowl is the staff's now.

name: 肉汁麺ススム 秋葉原本店
address_ja: 〒101-0021 東京都千代田区外神田3-7-12 イサミヤ第8ビル 1F
cuisine: The shop that invented 肉汁麺 — 3 mm-thick Spanish pork fried in a secret sweet tare and piled onto low-hydration medium-thick noodles with spring onion, served with a raw egg to dunk it in. You choose the meat: Level 1 (130 g), 2 (200 g), 3 (270 g) or MAX (800 g, eaten with special chopsticks and a ladle), plain or in the red 麻辣醤-and-sanshō version. Rice +¥100; the shop's own listed prices run ¥800–¥2,000, though that page dates from 2016 and Tabelog now bands it ¥1,000–¥1,999.
neighborhood: Soto-Kanda 3-chōme, on the 'junk street' side — 2 min from Suehirochō (Tokyo Metro Ginza line, exit 3), 5 min from JR Akihabara's Electric Town exit
gf_detail: Ruled out by the shop's own description, which is unusually specific about exactly the wrong things. The noodles are 「良質なブレンド小麦を低加水で練り上げ」 — a blended wheat flour, kneaded low-hydration. The soup's kaeshi is named outright as 本醸造こいくち醤油 from an old Japanese brewery: koikuchi shōyu is brewed on wheat, by definition. The pork is fried in a house 甘ダレ (a soy-based sweet tare) and the spicy version adds a fermented 麻辣醤 built on miso. Wheat is in the noodles, the soup and the meat glaze. No gluten-free claim and no allergen sheet.
vegan_detail: The name of the dish is 'meat-juice noodles' and the portion sizes are measured in grams of pork. On top of that the soup is 「動物系食材を贅沢にたっぷり使い」, a raw egg comes with every bowl by design, and the vegetable mix is finished with 背脂 (pork back fat). The 野菜肉汁麺 is more vegetables, not fewer animals.

roles: independent shop, opened 19 April 2016; owner not named publicly
chef_bio.origin: Soto-Kanda, Chiyoda-ku — the shop bills itself 秋葉原発祥, born in Akihabara
chef_bio.background: Susumu opened on 19 April 2016 in Soto-Kanda and invented a category: 肉汁麺, a bowl in which the pork is the portion size and the noodles are the support. The house line about it is knowingly ridiculous — 「欲求を抑えて生きる都会のおとこ達への禁断の贈りモノ」, a forbidden gift for city men who live suppressing their appetites — and the menu is built accordingly, with the meat sold by weight from 130 g up to an 800 g Level MAX that comes with its own chopsticks and ladle. Underneath the theatre is a fairly careful kitchen, and the shop's こだわり page is specific in a way most ramen sites are not: Spanish pork chosen for a clean, moist texture with the sourcing rotated by season, sliced to a fixed 3 mm because that is the thickness at which you taste the meat rather than chew it, then stir-fried with a house sweet tare so the fat and the char come out together; noodles of blended wheat kneaded at low hydration, rested properly and boiled short so they stay 「ポキっゴワっ」 against the meat; a kaeshi of 本醸造こいくち醤油 from a long-established brewery over a heavy animal stock; vegetables (negi, bean sprouts, kikurage, carrot, cabbage) cut coarse and blanched fast so they stay crisp, then bound with back fat; and for the red bowl a matured 麻辣醤 of miso and chilli lifted with sanshō. A second branch opened in Takadanobaba in May 2018. Thirty seats — fourteen at the counter and four four-tops — which for a shop of this type is generous, and it runs a single unbroken service from eleven in the morning to a quarter to nine, seven days a week. No chef is named; the shop's public face is the meat.
chef_bio.philosophy: Meat as the main event, quantified — the diner sets the weight of pork, and the noodle, soup and vegetables are engineered to hold it up.
chef_bio.specialty: 肉汁麺 Levels 1–3 (130 / 200 / 270 g) and Level MAX (800 g); 辛い肉汁麺 in the 麻辣醤+山椒 red soup; 肉汁つけ麺 (100–230 g); 野菜肉汁麺; the raw 「こだわり卵」 that comes with every bowl to dip the meat in.

anecdotes.text: Level MAX is 800 g of pork and is served with 「レベルMAX専用の特別な『箸とお玉』」 — its own dedicated chopsticks and ladle.
The shop fixes the pork at exactly 3 mm: thick enough to eat as meat, thin enough to take the sweet tare through in the pan.
Tabelog's listing carries the shop's own tagline verbatim — 「欲求を抑えて生きる都会のおとこ達への禁断の贈りモノ」.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Blended-wheat, low-hydration noodles boiled in a shared pot; no wheat-free item exists on the menu and no allergen information is published.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The shop names its own seasoning: the kaeshi is 本醸造こいくち醤油, which is brewed on wheat. The pork is also fried in a soy-based 甘ダレ, and the spicy tare is built on miso.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Pork by the hundred grams, an animal-heavy stock, a raw egg with every bowl, and pork back fat stirred through the vegetables.

positives.text: The shop publishes an unusually detailed ingredient page — flour type, hydration, soy-sauce type, pork origin, cut thickness — which is what makes the 'no' verdict here evidence rather than inference.

cultural_comfort.note: Straightforward once you know the one decision: how many grams of pork. Level 1 (130 g) is already a full meal by most standards; Level MAX (800 g) is a stunt and the shop treats it as one. Thirty seats with real tables as well as a counter, an unbroken 11:00–20:45 service seven days a week, and a location on the Suehirochō side of Akihabara that keeps it quieter than the shops right by the station. A raw egg arrives with the bowl — it is meant for dipping the meat, not for stirring into the soup. The shop's website is Japanese-only and partly broken, but the ordering itself is picture-and-number simple.
